guarantees.claim: wipe_secret is always assigned to reg2hw.wipe_secret.qe.
wipe_v is always assigned to reg2hw.wipe_secret.q.
digest_size_started_d is assigned digest_size when hash_start_or_continue is true, otherwise it is assigned digest_size_started_q.
key_length_supplied is assigned the type-cast value of cfg_reg.key_length.q to key_length_e.
err_valid is asserted when reg2hw.intr_state.hmac_err.q is low and any of hash_start_sha_disabled, update_seckey_inprocess, hash_start_active, msg_push_not_allowed, invalid_config_atstart is high.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.wipe_secret.qe and reg2hw.wipe_secret.q must correctly reflect a valid wipe command and value from the register interface.
assumptions.cond: when a secret wipe is intended
assumptions.risk: wipe_secret or wipe_v may not represent the desired wipe action, potentially leaving secret material uncleared.

assumptions.claim: cfg_reg.key_length.q must contain a legal key length value within the enumeration bounds of key_length_e.
assumptions.risk: key_length_supplied may be an invalid value, causing downstream state inconsistency or out-of-bounds behavior.

assumptions.claim: The error source signals (hash_start_sha_disabled, update_seckey_inprocess, hash_start_active, msg_push_not_allowed, invalid_config_atstart) must be asserted only on genuine error conditions.
assumptions.risk: False assertions on any input will cause err_valid to be incorrectly asserted, potentially triggering spurious error handling or masking a real error.

assumptions.claim: hash_start_or_continue must be stable when digest_size_started_d is sampled downstream.
assumptions.risk: Combinatorial glitches on hash_start_or_continue could cause the mux to select the wrong digest_size value, leading to an incorrect HMAC digest size being captured.

uncertain_points.claim: wipe_secret and wipe_v are driven directly from register fields, but their usage in the secret wipe logic is not visible. It is unclear if they are effectively used to gate actual wiping of secret material.
uncertain_points.risk: If these signals are unconnected or ignored, a secret wipe command may be silently dropped, leaving sensitive key material in registers.

uncertain_points.claim: err_valid asserts when update_seckey_inprocess is true and hmac_err is not active, but it is unclear whether this error alone is sufficient to halt or block further secret key operations.
uncertain_points.cond: when update_seckey_inprocess is high and reg2hw.intr_state.hmac_err.q is low
uncertain_points.risk: The HMAC may continue processing a secret key update despite a detected in-process error, potentially exposing or corrupting secret material.

uncertain_points.claim: key_length_supplied is a direct combinational wire from cfg_reg.key_length.q; if the register value changes while a key supply operation is in progress, the supplied key length may become inconsistent with the actual key data.
uncertain_points.cond: during key loading or while key length is assumed stable
uncertain_points.risk: A misaligned key length could lead to partial key acceptance, key truncation/expansion, or incorrect HMAC computations.
